rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials on the three tracks went off track with zero completions. Progress was only 0.11 to 0.16, each run had one line-loss event, and max_error (0.061 to 0.068 m) passed the 0.06 m off-track floor, while rms_error stayed near 0.03 m and steering oscillation was low (0.07 to 0.16). The robot tracks reasonably on average, then makes one large excursion, loses the tape, and the 0.35-throttle last_direction search carries it off. Base speed did not change the outcome: 1.2 to 1.8 all gave similar progress, so speed is not the main cause. The score is dominated by progress (250*progress plus a progress-weighted term), so staying on the line longer matters more than finish time, which is out of reach at this stage.

Changes: (1) Base speed lowered from 1.2 to 1.0 to reduce lateral drift in the fast bends. Even this is a modest cut, since a clean run at a slower speed is worth more than a fast run that leaves the track. (2) kp set to 2.0 and kd raised to 1.0 for stronger damping of overshoot at the edge. With edge signal of 2, turn is 4, which gives about 1400 PWM of differential, below the 2047 base PWM at speed 1.0, so the wheels do not reverse. (3) ki set to 0 to remove integrator windup on the bends. (4) Sensors moved to y = 0.05 m, 16 mm footprint kept, spacing 0.02 m across x = -0.04 to +0.04, so the array covers the tape at larger offsets while staying close to the axle for quicker reaction. (5) Mass reduced to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia so the body turns more readily. Geometry otherwise unchanged; line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error under 0.06 m on most seeds, and progress above 0.3 on the development tracks. Completion remains unlikely. The main risk is that the lower speed and extra damping slow the response enough to hurt rms_error; the revision round should check this.
